title: Terminal and Gravity
premise: Ulyana Sterling investigates impossible accidents along the relay route between Earth and the silent colony of Vesper-9, a world that severed contact decades ago and erased its own history. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream—a burning settlement, a locked reactor door—she realizes the 'accident' she's been hired to dismiss was a massacre the archives were rewritten to hide. As the reactor's automated countdown nears a catastrophic purge designed to destroy the last physical evidence, Ulyana must choose between her contract, her growing love for archivist Dario Kesh, and exposing a truth that would shatter the fragile peace keeping both worlds fed. She broadcasts the children's shared dream as living testimony seconds before the purge, sacrificing her invisibility and her safe passage home to give Vesper-9 its memory back.
about_author: Isandro Marchetti is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. Writing from a coastal town in southern Italy, Marchetti builds stories where paperwork hides ghosts and the truth is always a matter of who kept the records.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ulyana Sterling arrives at Vesper-9 aboard a freighter, hired by the Colonial Trust to close out an impossible claim: a settlement fire with no bodies, no debris, no records. Her POV establishes her rule of staying invisible. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking loneliness on a route no one else will fly.

chapters.title: A Town That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Ulyana walks the rebuilt settlement of New Halcyon, where residents answer questions with cheerful, identical vagueness. Archivist Dario Kesh is the only one who admits the archive has gaps. His POV alternates in. Emotional beat: uncanny warmth over something buried.

chapters.title: Claim Number 4471
chapters.summary: In the records vault, Ulyana finds the fire report dated twice, signed by a woman whose employment record ends the same day. Dario warns her some files are 'quarantined' by order of the Council of Continuity. Emotional beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: At the settlement school, Ulyana interviews witnesses for the claim and discovers nine children describe the same dream: a burning dormitory, a sealed reactor door, a voice counting down. Teacher Mira Solano begs her not to write it down. Emotional beat: dread dressed as coincidence.

chapters.title: The Reactor That Counts
chapters.summary: Dario shows Ulyana the old reactor complex, still running an automated maintenance cycle with a hard-coded purge sequence set to trigger in forty days. No one alive holds override authority. Emotional beat: a machine keeping a promise someone made long ago.

chapters.title: Tea with the Council
chapters.summary: Council head Odile Ferran hosts Ulyana graciously, offering full cooperation and a quiet hint that closing the claim fast benefits everyone—including her fare home. Ulyana recognizes the shape of a bribe. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon.

chapters.title: What the Ground Remembers
chapters.summary: Ulyana surveys the original burn site and finds soil chemistry inconsistent with any recorded fire—industrial accelerants, mass ash deposits. Someone cleaned the surface but not beneath it. Emotional beat: the thrill of proof, and the fear it brings.

chapters.title: Two Beds, One Lamp
chapters.summary: A dust storm strands Ulyana at the archive overnight. She and Dario trade stories about leaving worlds behind; he confesses he stayed because forgetting felt like mercy until she arrived. Emotional beat: intimacy kindling against duty.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Signed Twice
chapters.summary: Following the ghost signature, Ulyana locates Dr. Ilsa Rehn, the settlement's former medical officer, living exiled at the edge of the ice fields. Rehn agrees to talk—for a price Ulyana can't yet name. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Rehn's Testimony
chapters.summary: Rehn reveals the fire was a suppression operation: the first generation of colonists tried to shut down the reactor's behavioral compliance system, and the Trust's security detail burned the dissenters' block with everyone inside. The records rewrite was part of the settlement terms. Emotional beat: horror confirmed.

chapters.title: The Dream Is a Leak
chapters.summary: Ulyana realizes the children's shared dream matches Rehn's account exactly—the reactor's compliance system broadcast the massacre to its logs, and the logs are bleeding into the colony's neural-linked children. The dream is testimony the machines refused to erase. Emotional beat: awe turning to urgency.

chapters.title: Odile Knows
chapters.summary: Ferran summons Ulyana, no longer charming: she knows what Rehn said, and reveals the purge isn't just maintenance—it will wipe the reactor core, the last uncorrupted log, forever. She offers Ulyana passage home and a clean report. Emotional beat: threat wrapped in kindness.

chapters.title: The Weight of Leaving
chapters.summary: Ulyana drafts her closure report declaring the claim unfounded—and cannot send it. Dario, learning the full truth, struggles between protecting the colony's fragile peace and his love for her. Emotional beat: duty and love pulling opposite directions.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone torches Rehn's cabin; Ulyana arrives to find Rehn dead and her testimony recordings stolen. Only Ulyana's field notes remain. Grief hardens into resolve. Emotional beat: the price of knowing begins to be paid.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Days
chapters.summary: With the countdown public knowledge now, the colony splits: families demanding the truth, loyalists defending the peace that keeps supply ships coming. Ulyana becomes the axis both sides orbit. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership.

chapters.title: The Children Speak
chapters.summary: Mira brings the nine children to Ulyana voluntarily; together they reconstruct the full dream sequence, which contains coordinates and access phrases embedded by the dying reactor engineer who witnessed everything. Emotional beat: innocence carrying unbearable inheritance.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Ferran declares emergency protocol, detains Dario, and seals the archive. Ulyana escapes arrest through the storm drains with help from a loyalist guard who lost family in the fire. Emotional beat: hunted, alone, committed.

chapters.title: Into the Core
chapters.summary: Ulyana infiltrates the reactor complex during the final shift change, using the children's access phrases to reach the log chamber while the purge sequence enters its last hours. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Countdown
chapters.summary: Inside the core, Ulyana finds the raw logs—names, faces, final messages of the massacred—and must choose: copy them out slowly and risk the purge, or broadcast everything now through the colony's open child-link network, exposing herself to every law the Trust can throw at her. Emotional beat: the choice the whole book has built toward.

chapters.title: Terminal and Gravity
chapters.summary: Ulyana jacks the logs into the broadcast array as the purge fires; the massacre plays across every screen and mind on Vesper-9. Ferran's council collapses; the supply route goes dark. Ulyana, burned and half-blind from the surge, is pulled from the core by Dario. Emotional beat: catharsis through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the colony mourns publicly for the first time, holding names it finally remembers. The Trust sends investigators; Ulyana's testimony anchors their case. Dario chooses to stay and rebuild the archive honestly. Emotional beat: grief becoming foundation.

chapters.title: The Route Home
chapters.summary: Ulyana boards the first ship willing to fly, stripped of credentials but carrying the copied logs to Earth as evidence. The children wave from the dock, dreaming now only ordinary dreams. She looks back once—not invisible anymore, and no longer alone. Emotional beat: belonging earned at cost.
